target.title: fix(agents): pause yielded main-session runs
target.body:
## Summary

Extend the subagent yield-pause fix from [6f3b5f86](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6f3b5f8666f3a3877b62d9019b8842455fdf62e1) to top-level (non-subagent) sessions.

When a main session ends via the `sessions_yield` tool, the runner already emits a lifecycle event with `yielded: true` and `livenessState: "paused"`. The runner's terminal lifecycle metadata, the agent-job snapshot cache, and the agent.wait dedupe entry all propagate those flags generically, so subagent and non-subagent runs benefit equally from those parts of 6f3b5f86.

The gap is in `gateway/session-lifecycle-state.ts`. `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` does not look at the `yielded` flag, so the session entry is persisted with `status: \"done\"` even though the runner has queued a post-yield continuation that drains on the next turn. Dashboards, restart recovery, and follow-up turns then treat the session as finished and race the continuation, producing the in-context overflow and out-of-order events the user reports.

## Why the same fix needs to apply to the top-level session

The subagent registry tracks active subagent runs in memory and uses `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` to keep yielded entries in a paused state instead of marking them complete. The main session has no equivalent in-memory registry; its lifecycle state is persisted directly through `persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` into the on-disk session entry. The gap shows up in three places:

1. The persisted session entry says `status: \"done\"`, so `sessions_list`, `sessions.changed` broadcasts, and dashboard UI all show the session as finished.
2. `main-session-restart-recovery` is keyed off `entry.abortedLastRun` and `entry.status === \"running\"`. With status=done it leaves the entry alone, but on a clean restart-mid-yield the yielded session can also end up `abortedLastRun=true` (the cleaned-lock path), at which point recovery would force a `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted...` resume that races the queued continuation.
3. A new user message arrives at a session that is internally paused but externally \"done\" — the gateway dispatches a fresh agent.run, and the queued steered yield-interrupt drains alongside the new user input, producing out-of-order assistant text.

## Shape of the change

- Recognize the lifecycle `yielded` flag in `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` and derive `status: \"paused\"` with `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` instead of `done`. Yielded short-circuits before the `aborted`/`stopReason` branches so partial classifications cannot mask the paused state.
- Clear `pauseReason` on the next lifecycle `start` event so a fresh run reactivates the session, mirroring how `subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` clears `pauseReason` on completion.
- Add `\"paused\"` to `SessionRunStatus` in both `gateway/session-utils.types.ts` and `agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts`, and add `pauseReason?: \"sessions_yield\"` to `SessionEntry` and `GatewaySessionRow`.
- Surface `pauseReason` on the `sessions.changed` broadcast snapshot and the `loadGatewaySessionRow` builder so consumers (UI, sessions_list tool) see the paused state.
- Tighten `isTerminalSessionStatus` so the type predicate stays accurate after \"paused\" joins the union (paused is not terminal).
- Skip `main-session-restart-recovery` for entries with `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` so they are not re-prompted with the generic interrupted-turn message.

The runner-level changes (yieldDetected -> livenessState=paused/yielded=true) and the gateway agent-job/agent-wait-dedupe propagation that 6f3b5f86 already added are unchanged. This PR plugs the missing seam between those generic signals and the persisted session entry.

## Test coverage

- `src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts`:
  - `marks yielded lifecycle end events as paused with sessions_yield reason` (persisted patch).
  - `treats yielded as paused even when aborted is set` (yield short-circuit).
  - `clears pauseReason when a fresh run starts on a paused session` (start-phase reactivation).
  - Existing terminal-mapping tests updated to include explicit `pauseReason: undefined` on non-yield ends.
- `src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts`:
  - `skips sessions paused via sessions_yield instead of forcing a resume`.
  - `does not mark sessions with sessions_yield pauseReason as restart-aborted from cleaned locks`.

## Local validation

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts src/config/sessions.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.create-event.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent-wait-dedupe.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-output.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — all green (235 tests).
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm check:changelog-attributions` — all clean on changed files.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on \`fix(agents): pause yielded main-session runs\`.
- [ ] Manual smoke: trigger `sessions_yield` from a main-session conversation; confirm the session entry persists `status: paused` and `pauseReason: sessions_yield`, and that a follow-up turn flips back to `running` with `pauseReason: undefined`.
- [ ] Restart-recovery smoke: kill the gateway while a main session is paused via yield; confirm restart-recovery skips it instead of re-prompting with the interrupted-turn message.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Before this PR, when a top-level (non-subagent) embedded `openclaw` run ended via the `sessions_yield` tool, the runner emitted `yielded=true` and `livenessState=paused` but the gateway treated it as a clean completion and wrote `status=done`. The session displayed as finished while awaiting a queued post-yield continuation, racing dashboards, restart-recovery, and follow-up turns. After this PR, the lifecycle persistence derives `status=paused` with `pauseReason=sessions_yield`, restart-recovery skips paused sessions, and `SessionRunStatus` adds `"paused"` so consumers can distinguish a yielded run from a completed one.
- **Real environment tested**: live OpenClaw gateway on rh-bot.lan, pid 65734, build SHA 23804e610c (upgrade-v2026.5.28 with this PR cherry-picked). The deployed `dist/server-chat-*.js` and `dist/main-session-restart-recovery-*.js` chunks carry the new `pauseReason`/`sessions_yield` logic; the proof script imports and executes those exact bundle bytes.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  # On rh-bot.lan, confirm deployed bundles carry the PR logic:
  grep -c 'sessions_yield\|pauseReason' \
    /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js
  # -> 1 (the new shouldSkipMainRecovery branch)

  grep -c 'sessions_yield\|pauseReason' \
    /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js
  # -> non-zero (new deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot branches)

  # Drive the deployed code with three scenarios:
  node /tmp/proof-75662-amittell.mjs
  ```
  Proof script (`/tmp/proof-75662-amittell.mjs`) extracts the deployed
  `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` from `server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js` via
  `vm.runInContext`, dynamically imports `main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js`
  to grab the exported `markRestartAbortedMainSessions`, seeds a temp
  state-dir with one yielded and one non-yielded `running` entry, and asserts
  three behaviors:
  1. Lifecycle `phase=end` with `yielded=true` -> `status=paused`,
     `pauseReason=sessions_yield`, `abortedLastRun=false`.
  2. Same entry passed to restart-recovery is SKIPPED (no `abortedLastRun`
     write, `updatedAt` unchanged).
  3. Sibling running entry without `pauseReason` is marked
     `abortedLastRun=true` (existing behavior preserved).
  Plus a guard check: lifecycle `phase=error` with `yielded=true` returns
  `status=failed` with NO `pauseReason` leak.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  === PR #75662 real-behavior proof ===
  host=rh-bot.lan pid=84884 node=v25.8.2
  dist=/Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist

  [1] lifecycle bundle: /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js
  [1a] yielded terminal -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"paused","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false,"pauseReason":"sessions_yield"}
  [1a] OK: paused status carries pauseReason=sessions_yield
  [1b] non-yielded terminal -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"done","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false}
  [1b] OK: non-yielded run preserves status=done with no pauseReason
  [1c] error+yielded -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"failed","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false}
  [1c] OK: error phase masks yielded marker, no pauseReason leak

  [2] seeded /var/folders/cn/.../state/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
  [2] recovery bundle: /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js
  [2] exports: i, n, r, t
  [main-session-restart-recovery] marked 1 interrupted main session(s) for restart recovery (pr-75662-proof)
  [2] mark result: {"marked":1,"skipped":1}
  [2] yielded entry after: {"sessionId":"sess-yielded","status":"running","pauseReason":"sessions_yield","startedAt":...,"updatedAt":1780285519789}
  [2] normal entry after:  {"sessionId":"sess-normal","status":"running","startedAt":...,"updatedAt":1780285521266,"abortedLastRun":true}
  [2a] OK: yielded session was skipped (no abortedLastRun, no updatedAt bump)
  [2b] OK: non-yielded running session was marked abortedLastRun=true

  === ALL PROOFS PASSED ===
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: All three scenarios pass on the deployed bundle. A yielded terminal event produces `status=paused`/`pauseReason=sessions_yield` and is skipped by restart recovery (no `abortedLastRun` mutation, no `updatedAt` bump). A non-yielded terminal event still produces `status=done` with no `pauseReason` (existing behavior preserved). An error phase masks the `yielded` flag and reports `status=failed` with no `pauseReason` leak, matching the gating comment in `resolveTerminalStatus`.
- **Targeted tests**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts` -> 22 passed + 15 passed (37/37). Broader: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts` -> 172/172 passed. `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --only=core --threads=4` -> clean.
- **What was not tested**: End-to-end live channel trigger (sending a real Telegram message that drives `sessions_yield` to completion); this is exercised by the existing vitest coverage in `pi-embedded-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` rather than reproduced live on rh-bot.


## Live exact-head capture (2026-06-12): found and fixed an emit-side gap

Running the requested live scenario on an isolated sandbox gateway (loopback :28795, fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, Control UI webchat, native `openai-completions` lane with a tool-calling model) surfaced a real defect in this PR's original head: **the paused state never persisted in live runs, on any lane.** A store probe polling every 0.3s across four real `sessions_spawn` + `sessions_yield` turns at head `be96a422ff` captured the persisted row going `running -> killed` with `abortedLastRun: true` at yield time -- the exact pre-PR failure this PR exists to prevent.

**Root cause (probe-instrumented):** `sessions_yield` aborts the attempt mid-stream (`runAbortController.abort("sessions_yield")`), and the terminal lifecycle event can be emitted from the abort teardown before `run.ts` post-processing writes the `yielded` meta. The bundle-level instrumentation captured the failing ordering directly:

```
emitLifecycleTerminal state.yielded = undefined  aborted = false   <- event emitted first
meta.yielded set -> false                                          <- run.ts wrote 551ms later
```

The event reaches `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` carrying `aborted` without `yielded`, and `resolveTerminalStatus` correctly resolves killed. The projection/recovery/UI logic this PR adds was never the problem; the emit side never fed it. The unit tests passed because they fabricate events that already carry `yielded: true`.

**Fix (in `a46ba508b8`):** `onYield` now records `yielded` through the subscription's terminal lifecycle meta channel at tool time, before the abort, using the same late-binding pattern the yield abort itself uses (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`). A regression test pins the handler half: an end event with `state.yielded` set and `aborted` resolved from the `isTerminalAborted` fallback still carries `yielded` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.test.ts`).

**Post-fix live proof, end to end (same sandbox, instrumented bundle):**

```
10:27:40.065  [PROBE] meta.yielded set -> true              (onYield records at tool time)
10:27:40.423  [PROBE] emitLifecycleTerminal state.yielded = true   (event carries it)
10:27:4x      store: status=paused pauseReason=sessions_yield abortedLastRun=false
~10:28        Sessions Control UI: main session "Paused", subagent "Live"
10:28:1x      gateway KILLED while paused -> store unchanged (paused, ab=false)
10:28:3x      gateway restarted -> recovery skips the paused session;
              no "[System] Your previous turn was interrupted" prompt in the chat
10:29:20      subagent (orphan-recovered post-restart) completes -> announce drains
              the queued continuation in order -> running, pauseReason cleared
10:30:48      continuation finishes -> done, abortedLastRun=false
```

Reproduced again on a second pass (store probe `paused/sessions_yield` at 15:54-15:56 with closure-identity probes confirming the onYield-time recording). This covers all three asks: visible Paused state, restart skip, and orderly continuation, captured live at the exact head plus the one-commit fix.

**Codex lane now covered too (was a sibling-lane gap, now fixed in this PR).** The Codex app-server harness lane emits its own terminal lifecycle event (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts` `emitLifecycleTerminal`) and was dropping the yield meta: the `phase:"end"` event carried only `phase`/`aborted`, never `yielded`, so the shared projection (`resolveYielded`) persisted Codex-backed yields as done/killed. The fix forwards `{yielded, livenessState:"paused", stopReason:"end_turn"}` on that event when `result.yieldDetected`, exactly as the native runner does, gated on the flag the `sessions_yield` tool already sets via `onYield -> onYieldDetected`. The Codex lifecycle event flows through the same `onAgentEvent -> server-chat -> persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent -> resolveYielded` path as the native lane.

Proven live on the Codex lane: a real `openai/gpt-5.5` turn through the Codex app-server (ChatGPT OAuth) that calls `sessions_yield` now persists `status=paused`, `pauseReason=sessions_yield` (was `done` pre-fix), and the subagent then drains the queued continuation in order back to `done`. An integration test (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.yield-lifecycle.test.ts`) asserts the Codex lifecycle end event carries `yielded:true`/`livenessState:"paused"`/`stopReason:"end_turn"` on yield and omits them on a normal turn (verified red without the fix).

Codex protocol behavior checked against the sibling `../codex` source (HEAD `b8aea2340`): `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/ServerRequest.ts:19` defines the `{ "method": "item/tool/call", id, params: DynamicToolCallParams }` app-server -> client request, which is how the app-server invokes the OpenClaw `sessions_yield` dynamic tool (setting `yieldDetected`); turn lifecycle requests (`turn/start`/`turn/steer`/`turn/interrupt`) are at `ClientRequest.ts:90`. This change adds no new protocol dependency -- it forwards an OpenClaw-side flag onto OpenClaw's own lifecycle event.

## Summary
- add explicit intermediate active task states for approval waits and external waits
- propagate those active-state semantics across registry maintenance, flow guards, CLI views, and auto-reply task rendering
- add compressed operational summaries plus shared task lifecycle event formatting for state-change updates
- reuse the shared lifecycle formatter in task update delivery paths and extend focused task coverage

## Why
Previously, tasks moved through coarse active states like `queued` and `running`, which made it hard to distinguish between:
- work that is actively executing
- work that is alive but blocked on user approval
- work that is alive but waiting on an external dependency

This keeps the task model incremental while making the lifecycle more explicit and observable across the main task consumers.

## Notes
- intermediate task states are still projected as running at the `TaskFlow` layer for compatibility
- this PR also adds compressed operational summaries and lifecycle-oriented state-change formatting to make task progress easier to inspect across surfaces

## Testing
- OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test:fast -- src/tasks/task-status.test.ts src/tasks/task-executor-policy.test.ts
- OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test:fast -- src/tasks/task-status.test.ts src/tasks/task-executor-policy.test.ts src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts src/tasks/task-registry.store.test.ts

target.title: docs(rfd): @openclaw/call-sdk — provider-agnostic real-time call SDK
target.body:
## What

Adds an RFC + two companion design docs proposing **`@openclaw/call-sdk`** — a provider-agnostic real-time call SDK — and its binding into OpenClaw's `ChannelPlugin` model.

The three docs are intentionally split so each can be reviewed independently:

| File | What |
|---|---|
| [`docs/refactor/call-sdk-rfd.mdx`](https://github.com/visionik/clawdis/blob/rfc/call-sdk/docs/refactor/call-sdk-rfd.mdx) | RFC summary: goal, non-goals, proposed interface sketch, three hard tradeoffs. Entry point that links to the two companion docs. |
| [`docs/refactor/call-sdk-design.mdx`](https://github.com/visionik/clawdis/blob/rfc/call-sdk/docs/refactor/call-sdk-design.mdx) | Portable SDK API design: `Call`, `CallTransport`, `CallTap` and built-in tap kinds (`InferenceTap`, `RecordingTap`, `CaptionTap`, `IVRTap`, `TransformTap`, `MixerTap`, `TestTap`), `MediaFrame` v1→v2 plan, fan-out / `AbortSignal` as v1 core, lifecycle observability events, v1 / v1.1 / v2 / later scope split, worked examples, phased roadmap. |
| [`docs/refactor/call-sdk-channel-binding.mdx`](https://github.com/visionik/clawdis/blob/rfc/call-sdk/docs/refactor/call-sdk-channel-binding.mdx) | OpenClaw-side binding: `capabilities.call`, `ChannelPlugin.call: ChannelCallAdapter`, the load-bearing "channels never tap" guardrail (enforced at types / runtime / PR docs), authority/trust boundary between channels and tap-attaching code, two-axes / two-registries split, session-key conventions with `:call:<callId>`, `channel-call-inbound` dispatch helpers, single-connection contract, real-world capability matrix, 8-phase migration path. |

You can also browse all three in the [Files changed tab](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/73606/files).

## Why

OpenClaw handles dozens of messaging channels uniformly today. Real-time calls are not — every transport (WhatsApp calling, the in-progress Google Meet integration, Twilio voice) has its own ad-hoc wiring, no shared `Call` lifecycle, no standard way to attach STT/TTS, no recording, no captions. Every new transport reinvents the same patterns.

This RFC proposes the missing shared layer: a portable `@openclaw/call-sdk` exposing `Call` (per-call lifecycle and media surface) and `CallTap` (anything that consumes or produces media on a call), plus a thin OpenClaw binding (`ChannelPlugin.call: ChannelCallAdapter`) so a single channel package per platform can own both messaging and calls cleanly.

## Three hard tradeoffs (decided)

1. **`Buffer` v1, `MediaFrame` v2.** Ship `AsyncIterable<Buffer>` now to unblock the abstractions; design `MediaFrame` (codec / sample-rate / sequence / track / EOS / error) against real codec needs in v2.
2. **Multi-tap composition over single-bridge.** Many `CallTap`s per call, independent. Requires fan-out + `AbortSignal` cancellation to be boringly correct in v1 core, not v1.1 polish — otherwise detach leaks pipelines.
3. **Policy lives in the host, not the SDK.** `attachTap(call, tap)` is a plain function. OpenClaw wraps it as `core.attachTap(...)` under RBAC; the SDK exposes only attach/detach observability events for hosts to wire consent, audit, and recording-disclosure on top.

## Scope of this PR

**Docs only.** No code, no package added. The RFC asks for review of the design before any implementation begins; companion docs spell out the v1 / v1.1 / v2 / later split so reviewers can see the implementation-phase shape without that work being part of this PR.

## Open questions worth surfacing at RFD level

- Should `messaging` become optional on `ChannelPlugin` so call-only platforms (Meet, PSTN) are first-class? (Recommended: yes.)
- Should the plugin-sdk module path be `channel-call` (matches the renamed cap and SDK) or stay `channel-voice` (matches existing `realtime-voice` registry vocabulary)? (Recommended: `channel-call`.)

## External draft references

These docs were synthesized from in-progress drafts; gists kept until the RFD is merged for reviewers who want the change history:

- Call-SDK design gist: https://gist.github.com/visionik/e95177cc29fe5f9b8d7bb983635a520c
- Channel-plugin design gist: https://gist.github.com/visionik/6d27c758552403ea4b4641c72d73ebda

target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): resolve 200K context window for Claude 3.x and unlisted Anthropic Bedrock variants
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts` only listed a handful of Anthropic models in `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS`. Common Bedrock IDs such as `anthropic.claude-3-opus-20240229-v1:0`, `anthropic.claude-3-sonnet-20240229-v1:0`, and `anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-2024{0620,1022}-v{1,2}:0` fell through to `defaults.contextWindow` (32K by default), so prompts well below the model's actual 200K window tripped context-overflow precheck and triggered auto-compaction restart loops.
- Why it matters: every Bedrock customer using a Claude 3.x base model that wasn't already enumerated saw the gateway's in-memory model registry advertise 32K and refuse prompts the model could otherwise serve.
- What changed: backfill the missing Claude 3 / 3.5 / Opus 4 base entries at 200K, then add a small `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FAMILIES` table with an `^anthropic\.claude-(3|4)` regex so unlisted future variants and region-prefixed inference profiles (`us.anthropic.claude-*`, `jp.anthropic.claude-*`, etc.) default to 200K. Explicit table entries still win for higher-tier (1M) Claude rows.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no other vendor families. The `defaultContextWindow` config knob is untouched. Inference-profile prefix stripping logic and existing strict matches are unchanged.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope

- [x] amazon-bedrock plugin (provider discovery)

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #73328
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause

- Root cause: `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` was a hand-maintained map and missed the Claude 3 / 3.5 base IDs that most users encounter on Bedrock. There was no family-level fallback, so any unmatched model fell through to `resolveDefaultContextWindow` (32K default).
- Missing detection / guardrail: no test verified the family-level resolution; existing tests only cover Claude 3.7 / 4.x rows that happened to be in the map.
- Contributing context: AWS does not expose token-limit metadata via `ListFoundationModelsCommand`, so any unmatched model gets the conservative default.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts`
- Scenarios the test locks in:
  - Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 (`anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0`) resolves to 200K via the explicit table entry.
  - An unlisted future Claude 3 variant (`anthropic.claude-3-future-preview-v9:0`) resolves to 200K via the `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FAMILIES` fallback rather than 32K.
  - The same family fallback works for region-prefixed inference profiles (`us.anthropic.claude-3-future-preview-v9:0`).
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the bug surface is "missing entry / no fallback in `resolveKnownContextWindow`". The new tests pin both the table backfill and the family fallback, including the inference-profile prefix path.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Bedrock-discovered Claude 3.x models now report 200K context windows in the gateway's in-memory model registry instead of 32K.
- Bedrock-discovered Anthropic models with IDs not listed in `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` default to 200K via family fallback instead of 32K.
- No other providers are affected.

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

## Repro + Verification

### Steps

1. Configure a Bedrock provider with default discovery and a Claude 3.5 Sonnet (or any unlisted Claude 3.x) model.
2. Boot the gateway and inspect the in-memory model registry / `/health/deep`.
3. Send a prompt totalling ~16K input tokens.

### Expected

- `contextWindow` reported as 200000 for `anthropic.claude-*` Bedrock models, no context-overflow precheck triggered for the 16K prompt.

### Actual (before fix)

- `contextWindow=32000`; the 16K prompt is treated as nearly full and triggers `[context-overflow-precheck] estimatedPromptTokens=16300 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=15616` → `Auto-compaction failed.*Restarting session`.

## Evidence

- Static reproduction is provided by the new unit tests in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts`. Live Bedrock validation requires AWS credentials and is left to CI / downstream verification.

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: TypeScript clean on touched files; new tests added next to existing `discovery.test.ts` Claude/Sonnet suite.
- Edge cases checked: explicit table entries still win (e.g. Claude Sonnet 4.6 @ 1M), region-prefixed inference profiles route through stripping then family fallback, non-Claude families (Llama, Mistral, etc.) untouched.
- What I did NOT verify: a live Bedrock call with AWS credentials; full `pnpm check` / `pnpm test` was not exercised locally, leaving CI as the verification surface.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes — existing explicit table entries are unchanged. Only previously-incorrect 32K resolutions become 200K.
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: a non-Anthropic Bedrock model id happens to start with `anthropic.claude-3` or `anthropic.claude-4`.
  - Mitigation: AWS's Bedrock model id namespace is provider-prefixed (`anthropic.`), so this regex is well-scoped to the Claude family. The explicit map still takes precedence and any future tier-bump (e.g. another 1M variant) just needs another explicit entry.

target.title: feat(exec): inject OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID env vars for child processes
target.body:
## Summary
Inject `OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY` and `OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID` environment variables into child processes spawned by the exec tool, allowing scripts and skills to reliably identify the current session and agent without relying on model parameter passing.

Supersedes #68859 with full coverage including node-host execution, regression tests, and docs updates.

Closes #66705

## Problem
Currently, skills and scripts executed via exec have no reliable way to determine which session or agent they belong to. While the model can pass these identifiers as parameters, this approach is prone to hallucination errors where the model may provide incorrect values.

This blocks workflows where a child process needs to register a callback or webhook that routes back to the originating session.

## Solution
Automatically inject `OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY` and `OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID` into the environment of child processes spawned by exec, across all execution paths.

### Changes

**Core injection:**
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts` — inject both vars in `runExecProcess` (`shellRuntimeEnv`)
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts` — inject both vars in `shellRuntimeEnv` after sanitization for `host=node` execution
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts` — pass `agentId` through gateway allowlist path

**Type updates:**
- Added `agentId?: string` to `runExecProcess` opts type

**Documentation:**
- `docs/help/environment.md` — document both new env vars
- `docs/tools/exec.md` — note session/agent injection for all exec hosts

**Tests:**
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts` — 6 new tests covering gateway injection, user env override prevention, and empty-string clearing semantics
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — updated sanitizer allowlist test to verify trusted var injection
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts` — removed stale test (gateway no longer injects vars into `requestedEnv`)

## Testing
- [x] Local gateway execution (host=gateway)
- [x] Sandbox execution (host=sandbox) — covered by shared shellRuntimeEnv path
- [x] PTY mode (pty=true) — covered by shared shellRuntimeEnv path
- [x] Node-host execution (host=node) — unit tests in invoke-system-run.test.ts
- [x] Override semantics — user env cannot override trusted values
- [x] Clearing semantics — empty string when no agent/session defaults provided

## Usage Example
```python
import os
session_key = os.environ.get("OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY")
agent_id = os.environ.get("OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID")
```

## Backward Compatibility
Fully backward compatible:
- Variables always set (empty string when not available), avoiding stale-value issues
- Trusted values override any user-provided env overrides with the same names
- No existing behavior changed

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Inject OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID environment variables into exec child processes so skills and scripts can reliably identify their session and agent without relying on model parameter passing.

**Real environment tested**: OpenClaw 2026.4.2, macOS arm64, gateway mode

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
1. Built and ran OpenClaw gateway with the patched code
2. Created a minimal test skill at workspace/skills/test-env-injection/ that prints both environment variables
3. Executed the skill script via the exec tool within a main agent session
4. Captured the console output

**Evidence after fix**:
```bash
$ python3 ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/test-env-injection/test.py
agent:main:2
main
```

**Observed result after fix**: Both OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID are correctly injected into the exec child process environment. The output matches the expected session key (agent:main:2) and agent id (main).

**What was not tested**: Node-host (host=node) execution path was not tested in a real multi-node setup; only unit tests cover this path.

target.title: fix(exec-policy): accept trusted ~/.openclaw symlink at home boundary
target.body:
Fixes #72572.

## Problem

The exec-approvals symlink hardening from #72377 only relaxed the restriction on the `OPENCLAW_HOME` root itself, so a symlinked `~/.openclaw` immediate child of a real home directory still trips `assertNoSymlinkPathComponents()`:

\`\`\`
Refusing to traverse symlink in exec approvals path: /Users/funjim/.openclaw
\`\`\`

This breaks \`openclaw exec-policy preset yolo\` (and every other exec-policy command) for users who manage their OpenClaw config via GNU Stow, chezmoi, or any other dotfile-managed setup that exposes \`~/.openclaw → ~/dotfiles/openclaw/.openclaw\`.

## Fix

Allow EXACTLY ONE trusted symlink hop at the immediate child of the trusted home root, gated by the same hardening intent as #64050 / #72377:

1. Only the immediate child of the trusted root may be a symlink (deeper symlinks inside the resolved tree remain rejected).
2. The symlink target's realpath must be owned by the current effective user (\`process.geteuid()\`).
3. The symlink target must not be group- or other-writable (mode bits \`0o022\`).
4. After consuming the trusted hop, traversal continues from the realpath target with the original per-segment symlink rejection — a second symlink anywhere below is still rejected.

Permissive on platforms without \`process.geteuid\` (Windows), where the OS ACL model already differs.

\`ensureDir()\` is taught to accept a \`dir\` whose \`lstatSync\` reports a symlink, but only after re-asserting the realpath target is a directory — \`assertNoSymlinkPathComponents()\` already vetted ownership/perms.

## Tests

- **New**: \`accepts a symlinked ~/.openclaw immediate child of the trusted home\` — constructs the exact GNU Stow layout from the issue and verifies the file lands at the realpath target.
- **Updated**: \`refuses to traverse symlinked approvals components below a symlinked home\` — now constructs an unsafe (group-writable) symlink target so the deeper-symlink rejection intent of #72377 is still exercised. The original test became implicitly the same scenario as the new accept-test once the trusted-hop relaxation landed; making the target unsafe keeps the rejection branch under test.

All 18 \`exec-approvals-store\` tests pass; \`pnpm tsgo:test\` clean.

## Diff

+92 / -3 across 2 production files + 1 test file + CHANGELOG.

## Refs

- Original hardening: #64050
- Replaced PR (broader fix): #64663
- Merged narrow replacement: #72377
- This PR strictly broadens #72377 in the safe direction the issue describes.

target.title: fix(mcp): reject mixed command+url transport config (#72111)
target.body:
Closes #72111.

## Problem

When an MCP server config carries **both** a non-empty `command` and a non-empty `url` (e.g. a streamable-http endpoint plus a `command`/`args` pair), the runtime silently picks stdio and drops the HTTP transport. The user sees:

```
MCP server connection timed out after 30000ms
```

The spawned child never speaks JSON-RPC over stdio because the user actually wanted the streamable-http endpoint. The clawsweeper bot triaged this and recommended early rejection over silent fallback.

## Root cause

`resolveMcpTransportConfig` in `src/agents/mcp-transport-config.ts` resolves the stdio launch first when `command` is set, regardless of whether `url` is also set. The 30s timeout that follows is the user-visible symptom; the silent fallback at config-resolution time is the real bug.

## Reproducer

In `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`:

```json
{
  \"mcp\": {
    \"servers\": {
      \"broken\": {
        \"command\": \"node\",
        \"args\": [\"something.js\"],
        \"url\": \"https://my-mcp.example.com/mcp\"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Run OpenClaw → the `broken` server hangs, then errors with `MCP server connection timed out after 30000ms`. There is no clue in the logs about *which* transport was actually attempted.

## Fix

Reject the ambiguous shape early with a clear diagnostic that names the offending server and the requested transport hint, matching the file's existing \"skipped server X because Y\" diagnostic style and the clawsweeper bot's \"Best possible solution\":

> reject mixed `command` + `url`/HTTP transport configs early with a clear diagnostic and docs/test alignment. The current silent stdio precedence should not remain the user-visible timeout path.

Implementation: when `command` and a non-whitespace `url` are both present, log the warning, return `null` (caller already handles `null` as \"skip this server\"), and let the user fix their config.

Pure stdio configs (no `url`) and pure HTTP configs (no `command`) are unaffected. **Whitespace-only `url`** strings continue to be treated as \"no url\" so stdio still wins, matching the existing trimming in `mcp-stdio.ts`.

Diff: **+17** lines in `mcp-transport-config.ts`, **+52** in tests.

## Verification

```
pnpm vitest run src/agents/mcp-transport-config.test.ts
# 11 passed (7 original + 4 new)

pnpm check
# 0 errors, 0 warnings; all policy guards green
```

## Tests added (4 new)

1. **Mixed config + transport hint** → resolution returns `null`; warning lists both `command` and `url` and the requested transport.
2. **Mixed config without explicit transport hint** → still rejected; warning is informative.

target.title: fix(models): default input=[text,image] for vision-capable explicit-only models
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #71921.

When a user's `openclaw.json` contains a static model catalog for a provider (e.g. `amazon-bedrock`) and an entry omits the `input` field, `mergeProviderModels` previously returned that entry unchanged whenever discovery had no matching model to inherit from. Downstream `modelSupportsImages` (`dist/images-CzeTciMv.js`) reads `model.input?.includes("image") ?? false` — so `input === undefined` is silently treated as **text-only**, permanently breaking image attachments.

The full chain that produces this state in the wild:

1. `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts` imports from `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock`. That package is declared in the extension's `package.json` with `stageRuntimeDependencies: true` and is staged into `~/.openclaw/plugin-runtime-deps/.../node_modules/` on first boot after install/upgrade.
2. If OpenClaw resolves the amazon-bedrock catalog **before** runtime-deps staging completes, the import throws, discovery silently catches it, and returns no models.
3. In that empty-discovery state, a **static catalog** gets persisted into the user's `openclaw.json` for `models.providers.amazon-bedrock.models` — entries carrying `id`, `name`, `contextWindow`, `maxTokens`, but no `input`.
4. On subsequent boots, even after `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock` is installed and discovery works correctly, the user still carries that frozen static catalog. `mergeProviderModels` preserves each explicit entry verbatim when there's no matching implicit (discovery) entry, so `input` stays `undefined`.
5. User-visible effect: "Model does not support images" on every Bedrock Claude model, permanently, until the user manually edits `openclaw.json` or `~/.openclaw/agents/*/agent/models.json` to add `input: ["text", "image"]`.

## The fix

Teach `mergeProviderModels` to recognize vision-capable model ID patterns (Claude 3.5+/4.x, GPT-4o / 4.1 / 5 / o-series, Gemini 1.5+, Llama 3.2+ / 4.x vision families) and default `input: ["text", "image"]` when the user's explicit entry omits it and discovery has no match. Explicit entries that already specify `input` (including `input: ["text"]` to opt out of vision) are preserved unchanged, as are entries whose IDs don't match a known vision family.

This makes the merge behaviour "fail safe" for modern multimodal model families: if the user's static catalog is stale or incomplete, vision still works out of the box.

## What this does **not** attempt to fix

Three related issues from #71921 that felt out of scope for this PR — happy to follow up separately if maintainers want:

1. **Bundle `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock` directly** instead of staging via runtime-deps, to eliminate the first-boot race that seeds the stale static catalog in the first place.
2. **Refresh explicit catalogs when discovery later succeeds**, so stale entries don't linger forever.
3. **Add unknown-field warnings** in `planOpenClawModelsJson` when a static catalog is persisted without `input` for a model the provider could discover dynamically.

## Tests

New file: `src/agents/models-config.merge.explicit-input-default.test.ts`

- ✅ Defaults Claude Opus 4.x explicit-only entries to `[text, image]`
- ✅ Defaults Sonnet 4.x and Haiku 4.x explicit-only entries
- ✅ Defaults GPT-4o and Gemini 1.5+ families
- ✅ Preserves explicit `input: ["text"]` opt-out overrides
- ✅ Leaves non-vision / pre-vision model families (Titan embeddings, Claude 2, custom text-only) with `input` undefined
- ✅ Still inherits from implicit discovery when both catalogs contain the same model ID

All 6 tests pass locally. Existing `model-catalog.test.ts` and `models-config.*.test.ts` pass without regression.

## Reproduction / user workaround

Workaround for users hitting this before the fix ships:

```bash
python3 - << 'PY'
import json, pathlib
for p in pathlib.Path.home().glob('.openclaw/agents/*/agent/models.json'):
    d = json.loads(p.read_text())
    for m in d.get('providers',{}).get('amazon-bedrock',{}).get('models', []):
        mid = m.get('id','').lower()
        if any(k in mid for k in ['claude-opus-4','claude-sonnet-4','claude-haiku-4','claude-3-5','claude-3-7']):
            if 'image' not in m.get('input', []):
                m['input'] = ['text','image']
    p.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=2))

p = pathlib.Path.home() / '.openclaw' / 'openclaw.json'
d = json.loads(p.read_text())
for m in d.get('models',{}).get('providers',{}).get('amazon-bedrock',{}).get('models', []):
    mid = m.get('id','').lower()
    if any(k in mid for k in ['claude-opus-4','claude-sonnet-4','claude-haiku-4','claude-3-5','claude-3-7']):
        if 'image' not in m.get('input', []):
            m['input'] = ['text','image']
p.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=2))
PY
openclaw gateway restart
```

Tested end-to-end on OpenClaw 2026.4.24 with Claude Opus 4.7 on us-east-1 Bedrock.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Bedrock vision-capable models (Claude 3.5+/4.x, etc.) silently lose `input: ["text", "image"]` and downstream `modelSupportsImages` returns `false`, breaking image attachments. Bug from #71921. Reproduces whenever `mergeProviderModels` sees an explicit (static-catalog) entry without `input` and no matching implicit (discovery) entry to inherit from — exactly the state seeded after a first-boot race against `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock` runtime-deps staging.

**Real environment tested:** macOS 25.4.0 arm64 Mac mini, OpenClaw 2026.5.18 (commit 50a2481), Node 25.8.0, Claude Opus 4.7 via Amazon Bedrock `us-east-1` (model id `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`). Author's actual production OpenClaw install, not a sandbox.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

Step 1 — inspect the merged catalog state on the live install:

```bash
python3 -c "import json,pathlib;d=json.loads((pathlib.Path.home()/'.openclaw'/'openclaw.json').read_text());[print(m['id'],'input=',m.get('input','<<UNDEFINED>>')) for m in d['models']['providers']['amazon-bedrock']['models']]"
```

Step 2 — apply the merged regex from `src/agents/models-config.merge.ts` to 24 model IDs (12 vision-family + 12 substring-trap edge cases the unit tests guard). Full script linked under After-fix evidence.

Step 3 — end-to-end image attachment via Bedrock vision (real network call against `us-east-1`):

```bash
aws bedrock-runtime invoke-model \
  --model-id us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --body fileb://payload.json \
  --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out \
  /tmp/out.json
```

`payload.json` contains the multimodal message body (image + text content blocks).

**After-fix evidence:**

Live screenshot rendered and analyzed by Bedrock Claude Opus 4.7 in the same conversation:

![Real behavior proof — OpenClaw 2026.5.18, Bedrock Opus 4.7](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aaronedell/openclaw/64725aa8f591f1564eea044f0c7027d2bc43e8a9/.pr-proofs/72404/03-real-behavior-proof.png)

Linked terminal artifacts:
- Environment dump: [01-environment.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aaronedell/openclaw/64725aa8f591f1564eea044f0c7027d2bc43e8a9/.pr-proofs/72404/01-environment.txt)
- 24-case merge-regex verification (with output): [02-merge-logic-proof.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aaronedell/openclaw/64725aa8f591f1564eea044f0c7027d2bc43e8a9/.pr-proofs/72404/02-merge-logic-proof.txt)
- Live `aws bedrock-runtime invoke-model` transcript with token counts: [04-bedrock-vision-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aaronedell/openclaw/64725aa8f591f1564eea044f0c7027d2bc43e8a9/.pr-proofs/72404/04-bedrock-vision-live.txt)

Live Bedrock Opus 4.7 response (verbatim, from artifact 04):

```
=== Bedrock Claude Opus 4.7 response ===
**H1 title:**
OpenClaw PR #72404 — Real behavior proof

**Italicized note below it:**
Generated 2026-05-20 by Odin agent on Aaron's Mac mini (OpenClaw 2026.5.18, Claude Opus 4.7 via Bedrock us-east-1)

**Green check marks (✅) in the verification table:** 12

stop_reason: end_turn
input_tokens: 2228
output_tokens: 130
```

**Observed result after fix:** All 9 Bedrock Claude vision-family entries in the live `openclaw.json` carry `input=['text','image']` after the merge. The exact `VISION_CAPABLE_ID_PATTERNS` from the merged file produce the right answer for **24/24** real model IDs (12 vision → defaulted, 12 non-vision/edge cases → unchanged). End-to-end image attachment to `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` via `bedrock-runtime invoke-model` succeeds on the first call: model reads the PNG, quotes the H1 and italicized timestamp verbatim, counts the 12 ✅ checkmarks correctly, exits with `stop_reason: end_turn`, 2228 input tokens / 130 output tokens. Without this patch, `modelSupportsImages` returns `false` for these IDs and the attachment never reaches Bedrock.

**What was not tested:** (1) The first-boot runtime-deps race itself — that's the seeding mechanism described in the Summary and is out-of-scope for this fix (called out explicitly under "What this does not attempt to fix"). (2) Non-Bedrock providers (OpenAI, Gemini, Llama vision); their regex coverage is verified by the new unit tests but no live multimodal call was issued against them in this proof. (3) Re-running discovery to refresh stale explicit entries — also explicitly out-of-scope, listed as follow-up #2.

target.title: Fix/gateway silent revocation failures
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** Three bare `catch {}` blocks in the gateway WebSocket revocation paths (`server-shared-auth-generation.ts:28,43` and `server-request-context.ts:116`) silently swallow `socket.close()` failures. When an admin rotates gateway auth or removes a compromised device, a failing close leaves the evicted client connected with no log and no fallback.
- **Why it matters:** On the device-removal path, this is a fail-open security gap — an admin removes a compromised device, the close throws, the attacker keeps their authenticated WebSocket connection. The operator sees no indication that revocation was partial.
- **What changed:** Replaced all three bare catches with log-then-terminate: capture the error, warn with connId/deviceId/message, fall back to `socket.terminate()`. Extracted a shared `forceCloseSharedAuthClient` helper and `describeRevocationError` utility.
- **What did NOT change:** No changes to auth logic, pairing, session management, or any non-revocation paths.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Auth / tokens

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #70515 (same bare-catch pattern found in config recovery)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** Bare `catch {}` around `socket.close()` in three revocation loops.
- **Missing detection / guardrail:** No test injected a throwing `socket.close()` on the revocation path.
- **Contributing context:** The catch structure is intentional (rethrowing would kill the eviction loop for sibling clients), but the silent swallow is not.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: [x] Unit test
- **Scenario:** Inject a throwing `socket.close`, assert (a) `logger.warn` fires with connId + error message, (b) `terminate()` is called as fallback, (c) remaining clients in the iterable still get evicted.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Operators now see a warning log when a revocation close fails. Failed closes fall back to `socket.terminate()` — the evicted client is now force-killed even when the graceful close throws.

## Diagram

```text
Before:
[socket.close() throws] -> [catch {}] -> [attacker keeps connection] -> [no log]

After:
[socket.close() throws] -> [warn log with connId + error] -> [socket.terminate()] -> [connection killed]
```

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Bare `catch {}` blocks around `socket.close()` in the three gateway WebSocket revocation paths silently swallowed failures. When a device removal or shared-auth rotation triggered a close that threw, the evicted client stayed connected with no log and no fallback — a fail-open security gap on the device-removal path.

**Real environment tested:** macOS 25.4.0 / Node 23.7.0, project source checkout, `node --import tsx/esm` run directly against the call-chain pattern.

**Exact steps or command run after the patch:**
```
node --import tsx/esm proof-70676.mts
```

**Evidence after fix:**

Before the fix (bare `catch {}`):
```
=== BEFORE FIX (bare catch {}) ===
  Warned: none (silent failure)
  Terminated as fallback: none — conn-bad may still be connected!
```

After the fix (warn + terminate fallback):
```
=== AFTER FIX (warn + terminate fallback) ===
  Warned: "revocation close failed for connId=conn-bad: Error: socket already destroyed — attempting terminate()"
  Terminated as fallback: conn-bad ✓ — attacker connection killed
  conn-healthy untouched: yes ✓
```

**Observed result after fix:** Failed revocation closes now log a warning with the `connId` and error message, fall back to `socket.terminate()` to force-kill the connection, and continue evicting remaining clients in the loop. The fail-open gap is closed.

**What was not tested:** Full integration test with real WebSocket in half-closed state. The `node` script above isolates the exact three-branch pattern and produces real before/after terminal output demonstrating the silent failure and its fix.

target.title: Test/run state machine clamp guard
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: The `activeRuns` clamp guard in `onRunEnd()` (`Math.max(0, activeRuns - 1)`) was completely untested. Calling `onRunEnd()` more times than `onRunStart()` (e.g. error handling paths, race conditions) would cause `activeRuns` to go negative without this guard.
- Why it matters: A negative `activeRuns` would cause the machine to report incorrect state permanently, potentially breaking busy indicators across all channels.
- What changed: Added two unit tests covering the clamp guard — one for calling `onRunEnd()` with no prior `onRunStart()`, and one for calling it more times than `onRunStart()`.
- What did NOT change: No production code was changed. This is a test-only PR covering an existing defensive guard.

## Change Type (select all)

- Missing detection / guardrail: No unit test for mismatched `onRunStart`/`onRunEnd` calls.
- Contributing context (if known): Error handling paths or race conditions can trigger `onRunEnd()` more times than `onRunStart()`.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)
- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test

- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Pure function, no dependencies, directly tests the guard condition.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[onRunEnd x2] -> activeRuns = -1 (without guard, would break busy state)

After:
[onRunEnd x2] -> activeRuns = 0 (guard clamps correctly, now verified by test)
```

## Security Impact (required)

target.body:
## Fix Summary
The `deriveInteractionSecret` function in the Mattermost extension uses a hardcoded public string as the HMAC key, making the interaction signing secret fully reproducible by anyone who knows the bot token. An attacker who obtains the bot token can forge valid `_token` values, craft arbitrary button-click POST requests to the gateway's interaction endpoint, and trigger agent system events (`core.system.enqueueSystemEvent`) as if a legitimate user clicked an approved Mattermost button.

## Issue Linkage
Fixes #64545

## Security Snapshot
- CVSS v3.1: 7.1 (High)
- CVSS v4.0: 7.1 (High)

## Implementation Details
### Files Changed
- `extensions/mattermost/src/config-schema-core.ts` (+1/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/config-schema.test.ts` (+19/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/accounts.test.ts` (+23/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/accounts.ts` (+8/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.test.ts` (+20/-17)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.ts` (+23/-10)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts` (+2/-3)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.ts` (+8/-2)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/types.ts` (+2/-0)

### Technical Analysis
1. Obtain the Mattermost bot token (available via the Mattermost admin panel, gateway environment variables, or any configuration leak).
2. Reproduce the derivation: `derivedSecret = HMAC-SHA256("openclaw-mattermost-interactions", botToken)` — this is deterministic and requires no further gateway access.
3. Construct an action context matching an existing interactive post, e.g., `{"action_id": "approve", "post_id": "<target_post_id>", "channel_id": "<target_channel_id>"}`.
4. Compute the forged token: `_token = HMAC-SHA256(derivedSecret, JSON.stringify(sortedContext))`.
5. POST a crafted payload to `http://<gateway-host>:<gatewayPort>/mattermost/interactions/<accountId>` with the forged `_token` field.
6. `verifyInteractionToken` at `interactions.ts:165-175` passes; the handler dispatches `core.system.enqueueSystemEvent` to the agent as if a legitimate user clicked an approved button.

## Validation Evidence
- Command: `pnpm exec oxlint src/ && pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test`
- Status: passed (with pre-existing baseline failures)

## Risk and Compatibility
- non-breaking; no known regression impact

## AI-Assisted Disclosure
- AI-assisted: yes
- Model: github-copilot/claude-sonnet-4.6

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Mattermost interaction tokens should no longer be forgeable from knowledge of the bot token; the branch now uses a generated or configured interaction secret instead of the old deterministic `HMAC-SHA256("openclaw-mattermost-interactions", botToken)` derivation.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on the rebased PR head `e261bcfab6de7ff05d18d2493ea60aedf234498d`, running the real Mattermost interaction module through Node with `tsx`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e 'import { createHmac } from "node:crypto"; import { ensureInteractionSecret, generateInteractionToken, verifyInteractionToken } from "./extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.ts"; const botToken = "redacted-bot-token-for-proof"; const oldDerivedSecret = createHmac("sha256", "openclaw-mattermost-interactions").update(botToken).digest("hex"); const generatedSecret = ensureInteractionSecret("proof-account"); const configuredSecret = ensureInteractionSecret("configured-account", "configured-proof-secret"); const context = { action_id: "approve", proof: "after-fix" }; const validToken = generateInteractionToken(context, "proof-account"); const oldForgedToken = createHmac("sha256", oldDerivedSecret).update(JSON.stringify(context)).digest("hex"); console.log(JSON.stringify({ generatedSecretLength: generatedSecret.length, generatedSecretIsHex: /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/.test(generatedSecret), generatedSecretMatchesOldBotTokenDerivation: generatedSecret === oldDerivedSecret, configuredSecretPreserved: configuredSecret === "configured-proof-secret", generatedTokenVerifies: verifyInteractionToken(context, validToken, "proof-account"), oldBotTokenDerivedForgeryVerifies: verifyInteractionToken(context, oldForgedToken, "proof-account") }, null, 2));'
```

- Evidence after fix:

```json
{
  "generatedSecretLength": 64,
  "generatedSecretIsHex": true,
  "generatedSecretMatchesOldBotTokenDerivation": false,
  "configuredSecretPreserved": true,
  "generatedTokenVerifies": true,
  "oldBotTokenDerivedForgeryVerifies": false
}
```

- What was not tested: Full live Mattermost server button-click delivery was not exercised in this local proof; focused local runtime proof and Mattermost extension tests were run for the changed interaction-secret behavior.

## Summary
Adds a `runtime.usage` namespace to the plugin runtime, exposing `resolveModelCostConfig()` and `estimateUsageCost()` so context engine plugins can calculate model-cost estimates from OpenClaw's configured pricing instead of hardcoded heuristics.

## Motivation
Context engine plugins, such as [ContextClaw](https://github.com/dodge1218/contextclaw), truncate stale or large context to save tokens. Today they can only estimate savings with a fixed heuristic. OpenClaw already has per-model pricing through `resolveModelCostConfig`; this PR threads those helpers through the plugin runtime so plugins can use the same pricing source as the host.

target.title: feat: Provider circuit breaker for quota exhaustion
target.body:
Resolves #64085

This PR introduces proper handling for daily/weekly/monthly quota exhaustion errors:
1. Detects periodic usage limits and classifies them as `"quota_exhausted"` (rather than transient `rate_limit`).
2. Routes `quota_exhausted` through the same persistent backoff lane as billing failures (bypassing the provider for 5-24 hours).
3. Adds a new `agent:provider_tripped` internal hook event whenever a provider enters the disabled lane, allowing plugins (like ContextClaw) to observe and react to provider death.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: OpenClaw previously treated periodic quota-exhaustion messages as ordinary transient rate limits, so a provider that had exhausted a daily/weekly/monthly usage window could keep being retried through the short rate-limit lane. This patch classifies those cases as `quota_exhausted`, routes them through the long disabled-lane backoff, and emits `agent:provider_tripped` when a provider enters that disabled lane.

- Branch/head: `feat/provider-circuit-breaker` at `6f2493db9043f43a30a0b59def58a9d37206a222`, then lint-only follow-up applied locally before push.

- Before-patch incident context: ScientificProgrammer reported a real OpenClaw deployment where a Gemini monthly spending-cap condition produced repeated `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` cascades across 26 runIds and about 390 exhausted-provider events.

target.title: fix: accept valid MCP tool schemas without strict inputSchema.type check
target.body:
## Summary
Fixes MCP server loading failure when tools have `inputSchema` without explicit `type: "object"`.

Closes #63602

## Changes
- `listAllTools` validates each `tools/list` page **once** with `RelaxedListToolsResultSchema` and catalogs **that same validated payload** — there is no strict-then-relist flow, so a stateful or hostile server cannot pass validation with one response and have a different response consumed (no validation-to-use gap).
- `RelaxedToolSchema` is **derived from the pinned SDK's own `ToolSchema`** (`ToolSchema.extend` / `ToolSchema.shape.inputSchema.extend`) and differs from it at exactly one point: the root `inputSchema.type` is an optional string instead of `z.literal("object")`. Every other field — `outputSchema`, task `execution` metadata, `annotations`, pagination — keeps the exact pinned SDK contract, so malformed metadata still rejects the page.
- After every page parse, the SDK's `cacheToolMetadata()` is invoked with the validated tools — the same side effect `client.listTools()` runs — so `callTool()` enforces output-schema validation and task-required guards identically to the SDK flow. The call is optional (no crash if a future SDK removes the method) and a dedicated test pins the method's existence so a dependency upgrade that drops it fails loudly rather than silently shedding the guards.
- `normalizeInputSchema()` backfills `type: "object"` only when the field is missing; `isValidRootInputSchema()` + the catalog gate skip tools with an explicit non-object root type (e.g. `"string"`, `"array"`) with a `logWarn`. Server `toolCount` reports accepted tools only.

## Root Cause
The MCP SDK v1.29.0 `ToolSchema` validates `inputSchema.type` as `z.literal("object")`. Some MCP servers (especially older SDKs or custom implementations) omit `type` from `inputSchema`, returning `{ properties: { ... } }`, which trips a Zod validation error: `invalid_value expected "object" in inputSchema.type` and crashes the whole catalog.

## v6 notes (current revision)
Addresses the P1 from the latest review (validation-to-use gap, confidence 0.96) by adopting its recommended repair: single-response validation that differs from the pinned SDK `ToolSchema` only at the root `inputSchema.type`, with SDK-equivalent metadata caching, explicit non-object filtering, and pagination preserved.
- The strict-then-relist flow is gone entirely; the request count per page is 1 in all cases.
- New stateful-server regression: a server that returns a benign typeless payload on request 1 and a malicious payload on request 2 gets exactly one `tools/list` request, and only the validated payload is cataloged. **Mutation-checked**: against the previous strict-then-relist implementation this test fails with the catalog containing the drifted (never-strictly-validated) tool — reproducing the reported attack — and the server log showing two list requests.
- New SDK-seam pin test: `Client.prototype.cacheToolMetadata` must exist, making the documented private-method dependency an explicit, loudly-failing audit point on SDK upgrades (P1 risk #2 from the same review).
- Relaxation-scope unit tests: malformed `outputSchema`, malformed `execution.taskSupport`, and missing `inputSchema` all still reject the page; pagination (`nextCursor`) keeps the SDK contract.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior or issue addressed: Bundle MCP tool cataloging accepts tools whose root `inputSchema` omits `type` by validating each `tools/list` response once against a schema derived from the pinned SDK contract (relaxed only at the root `inputSchema.type`), backfills `type: "object"`, skips explicit non-object roots, keeps servers with unrelated strict failures rejected, never issues a second list request, and preserves the SDK's `cacheToolMetadata()` side effects for every page.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS from the rebased PR head, Node 25.2.1, pnpm 11.2.2, driving the real bundle MCP runtime (`getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime` → `getCatalog()` → `callTool()`) against four real out-of-process stdio MCP servers, one of them stateful (different payload per request).

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran `pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`, and `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1` on both files, plus a live four-server e2e script via `pnpm exec tsx`.

Evidence after fix:
```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  42 passed (42)
pnpm tsgo:core / tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint / oxfmt --check: clean

e2e (four live stdio servers):
tools: ["legacySdkServer/search_docs","driftServer/benign_typeless_tool"]
servers: {"legacySdkServer":{"toolCount":1},"driftServer":{"toolCount":1}}
rejected: ["badOutputServer","mixedServer"]
driftServer tools/list requests received: 1        // exactly one — no second-request window
callTool(search_docs) → McpError -32600: Tool search_docs has an output schema but did not
  return structured content                        // metadata cache populated from the same response
```

Observed result after fix: A `tools/list` payload whose `inputSchema` omits `type` catalogs cleanly with `type: "object"` backfilled; an explicit `type: "array"` sibling is skipped with a logWarn; servers with malformed `outputSchema` (alone or mixed with a repairable tool) stay rejected; a stateful server attempting response drift receives exactly one list request and only its validated payload is cataloged; `callTool()` enforces `outputSchema` for typeless tools exactly as the SDK strict flow would.

What was not tested: A live third-party MCP server connected to an actual model-provider tool call was not tested in this environment.

target.title: fix(gateway): use already-aborted signal in stopChannel fallback
target.body:
## Summary

- In `stopChannel`, when no `AbortController` exists for an account (i.e. no running task), the fallback `new AbortController().signal` creates a signal from an anonymous controller that **can never be aborted**
- `stopAccount` implementations may use this signal for cleanup coordination (checking `signal.aborted`, passing to `fetch`, using with `sleepWithAbort`, etc.)
- A never-aborting signal can cause `stopAccount` to hang or timeout during graceful shutdown instead of completing immediately

### Fix

Replace `new AbortController().signal` with `AbortSignal.abort()`, which returns an already-aborted signal. This correctly communicates "this account is being stopped" to the plugin's `stopAccount` implementation.

### Context

On line 485, `abort?.abort()` is called — so if `abort` exists, its signal is already aborted. The fallback only fires when `abort` is undefined (no active task for this account). In both cases the intent is the same: tell `stopAccount` to shut down. `AbortSignal.abort()` makes the fallback consistent with the primary path.

## Test plan

- [x] All 14 tests in `server-channels.test.ts` pass
- [x] One-line change, minimal risk
- [x] `AbortSignal.abort()` is available since Node 15.12.0; project requires Node 22+

target.title: fix(moonshot): kimi search 401 with china-region api keys
target.body:
Closes #94979

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with China-region Moonshot API keys receive 401 Invalid Authentication from Kimi web search when no explicit search base URL is configured. The same API key works correctly for Moonshot chat completions, but fails for web search because the default search endpoint (`api.moonshot.ai`) does not accept China-region keys. Users with custom chat proxy endpoints also encounter the same problem when no separate search base URL is set.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is a documentation and discoverability gap, not a code logic defect. The existing `isNativeMoonshotBaseUrl` guard is an intentional security boundary to avoid routing search credentials to unvetted custom endpoints that may not support Moonshot's `$web_search` API. This PR closes the information gap with three targeted, non-breaking improvements, without changing any core routing or inheritance behavior:

- Documentation updates to highlight region-specific base URL requirements and explicit proxy configuration rules
- Enhanced 401 error messages with actionable troubleshooting guidance
- Full preservation of the existing guard, fallback order, and onboarding flow

## User Impact

- Users with China-region Moonshot API keys can find the correct base URL configuration directly from the Config example and note, without needing to file an issue.
- Users with custom Moonshot-compatible proxies have clear documented guidance via the new Base URL overrides section, and receive actionable next steps in 401 error messages.
- Existing users using official native endpoints (`.ai` or `.cn`) experience no change in behavior.

## Evidence

- **15/15 tests pass with zero modifications** — no regressions; the existing test asserting "custom proxy base URLs are not inherited" remains valid and unchanged.
- **Consistent with all 12 bundled search provider docs** — all use `plugins.entries.*.config.webSearch.*` as the canonical configuration path.
- **Base URL overrides section aligns with Gemini** (`docs/tools/gemini-search.md:102-109`) and **Grok** (`docs/tools/grok-search.md:117-123`) in structure and wording.
- **401 error enhancement follows Ollama's established pattern** (`extensions/ollama/src/web-search-provider.ts:202`) of including actionable diagnostics in error messages.
- **Test output:** `pnpm test extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.test.ts` → all 15 tests passed.
- **Diff:** 2 files, ~+21 lines. No changes to core routing, `isNativeMoonshotBaseUrl`, config schema, or onboarding.

target.title: fix(usage): handle Daylight saving time (DST) hour boundaries
target.body:
## Summary

This fixes a Control UI Usage-page freeze when a long session spans a local Daylight saving time (DST) transition.

Today the hour-slicing code computes a local `:59:59.999` hour end from the current wall-clock time. In a repeated local hour at Daylight saving time (DST) fallback, that can resolve to an earlier instant and stop cursor progress.

This change switches Usage hour slicing and selected-hour filtering to monotonic next-hour-boundary stepping so aggregation always moves forward in the selected timezone.

## Why

This fixes cases where:

- Usage is rendered in local time
- a session spans a Daylight saving time (DST) fallback or spring-forward boundary
- the page builds hour buckets or applies a selected-hour filter

Without this change, the Control UI can wedge the browser main thread while rendering Usage data for long sessions.

## Changes

- replace the ambiguous local end-of-hour calculation with `getNextHourStart()` plus bounded next-hour stepping in `ui/src/ui/views/usage-metrics.ts`
- convert session hour slicing to half-open intervals `[cursor, nextBoundary)` so exact boundaries do not create zero-duration buckets
- route the selected-hour filter in `ui/src/ui/views/usage.ts` through the same DST-safe helper instead of maintaining a duplicate loop
- add focused node-side regression coverage for Daylight saving time (DST) fallback, Daylight saving time (DST) spring-forward, peak-error aggregation, and full Usage render with an hour filter

## Testing
